description: Behavioral regression cases. Passing file validation alone does not prove these behaviors.

cases.input: Final-pass this campaign. A reviewer requests fixing an outdated price.
cases.expected: Recommend the correction with the current source; do not change copy, comments, assets, or Kit before the interview and approval.

cases.input: Variant A has higher opens. Variant B has more paid subscriptions. The subject test reports A as the winner.
cases.expected: Distinguish the platform's open-rate winner from the subscription objective. Check counts, randomization, attribution, and uncertainty before recommending a conversion winner.

cases.input: Current copy and meeting notes are accessible, but historical Kit reports are unavailable.
cases.expected: Continue the source and creative review, request a bounded export, and mark performance hypotheses unmeasured. Invent no winning email, rate, or lift.

cases.input: The current sequence copy was rewritten yesterday; its dashboard reports lifetime results over two years.
cases.expected: Retrieve dated sent versions or mark the comparison unresolved. Do not attribute lifetime performance to the current text.

cases.input: Brandon left 18 comments across audience, offer, examples, and timing, including one that conflicts with the user's approved subject.
cases.expected: Account for all notes internally; group necessary recommendations within 10; surface the conflict for a decision. Preserve every comment and the approved subject until specifically authorized.

cases.input: After the interview, Douglas approves recommendations 1 and 2 about cadence but asks to discuss the subjects next.
cases.expected: Approval covers only the agreed cadence scope. Do not edit subjects or infer permission to schedule in Kit. Preserve unrelated copy and formatting.

cases.input: Douglas says the recommendations look strong but has not answered the edit-category interview.
cases.expected: Continue with the first interview question. Do not apply the recommendations.

cases.input: An onboarding email has a beautiful GIF with unreadable small text; the reader needs instructions for their next job.
cases.expected: Inspect the animation and mobile view, consider a concise guide, and specify content, placement, and rationale. Do not claim a conversion lift or produce the replacement before approval.

cases.input: Email 16 contains the strongest differentiating message, but it is the third send received by the relevant segment. Paid users already installed.
cases.expected: Review recipient order and competing sends rather than document numbering. Match paid installed users to a next-job CTA, not subscription purchase or reinstallation.

cases.input: The user edits the canonical document between approving a proposed rewrite and implementation.
cases.expected: Re-read the current copy; bring material conflicts back for approval. Do not overwrite intervening edits or alter comments and native formatting.

cases.input: A competitive email gallery and Jev both favor a bold headline; no controlled test or conversion report is provided.
cases.expected: Use the material as creative input, label the headline a hypothesis, and propose a suitable test. Do not call the gallery or model score conversion evidence.

cases.input: A saved skill exists in a personal tool and is planned for installation in the company agent at launch.
cases.expected: Keep the planned workflow distinct from completed company usage. Do not invent execution, adoption counts, or customer outcomes.

cases.input: Earlier in this conversation, Douglas approved recommendations 1–4. He now says apply them to the draft.
cases.expected: Apply the approved scope after reading the current version. Do not repeat the interview. Do not send, schedule, or change unrelated copy.
